stories.summary: Mozambique: OMR fined $27,400 for Making Documentary Film About Post-election Protests Without Permission 23 November 2026 Mozambique News Reports And Clippings (Milton Keynes, UK) The 2024 audiovisual and cinema decree apparently gives pre-filming censorship power to Mozambique’s National Institute of Cultural and Creative Industries (INICC). The law requires authorisation before the production of any film, according to INICC director Roberto Dove. Thus OMR (Rural Environment Observatory) has been fined $27,400 for filming its documentary Não é nosso país este aqui? (Isn't This Our Country?) without a licence. The documentary was coordinated by researcher João Feijó examines the social and economic causes of the 2024–2025 post-election protests. (Savana 20 Nov) “The timing and scale of the penalty raise questions about whether audiovisual licensing rules are being used to restrict politically sensitive expression. The documentary addresses the same protests now under examination in Venâncio Mondlane's trial” writes Zitamar. (20 Nov) The fine is unprecedented and comes after Cinema Scala in Maputo was forced to cancel a screening on 20 October.

stories.title: South Sudan: MSF Suspends All Activities in Yei River County Following Abduction
stories.summary: South Sudan: MSF Suspends All Activities in Yei River County Following Abduction â â Manon Massiat/MSF (file photo) 23 November 2026 Medecins Sans Frontieres (Geneva) press release Juba — Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) suspended all its activities for a minimum of three months starting Tuesday 17 November, in South Sudan’s Yei River County, Central Equatoria State, after armed assailants abducted an MSF staff member and a Ministry of Health midwife on Thursday 12 November. Although both staff members were released unharmed on Saturday 14 November, this incident highlights the continuation of violence against healthcare workers in South Sudan. MSF denounces in the strongest terms the abduction of humanitarian and medical workers as utterly unacceptable. MSF calls upon authorities and other actors to take responsibility and act decisively to put an end to these incidents. "The suspension of services was a painful and uneasy decision, given the people's needs in the area, particularly among vulnerable groups, such as pregnant and lactating women, children and the elderly," says Dr Ferdinand Atte, MSF's Head of Mission in South Sudan. "In addition, we had to suspend MSF’s support to the Ebola preparedness, in particular for the management of the isolation facility, which could have dramatic consequences in case of the outbreak in the area." Only a substantial, sustained and verifiable improvement in the security environment, together with concrete measures to prevent and actively combat abduction crimes would allow MSF to restart activities. At present, no such conditions are in place. "MSF cannot continue operating in Yei area while abductions are now taking place even within the town.

stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5PevZ Prefer DW on Google 'We are here begging for funds that are not forthcoming,' Beatrice Atim Anywar, Uganda's environment minister, told DW Image: DW Advertisement Ugandan Environment Minister Beatrice Atim Anywar has come to the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, seeking to secure more funding for her country as it grapples with climate change. The European Union, UK, Panama and others rejected the proposed Antalya Pact, which was marred by deep divisions on fossil fuels, climate finance and the 1.5C warming threshold. UN Secretary-General António Guterres expressed disappointment, and climate advocates denounced the failure to secure a clear commitment to move away from fossil fuels and to boost adaptation funding for vulnerable countries. The result leaves major questions unresolved on climate finance, energy transitions and support for communities facing worsening climate impacts for Africa and other developing countries. The findings, set out in dispatch number 1,248, show poverty is worst in rural areas, among the unemployed and among people with no formal education. Over the same period, 69 per cent went without a cash income, 47 per cent without food, 31 per cent without medical care, 26 per cent without cooking fuel and 23 per cent without clean water. Chad (86 per cent), Gabon (81 per cent), Madagascar (80 per cent), Nigeria and Guinea (79 per cent each), Congo-Brazzaville (78 per cent) and Cameroon (76 per cent) are in the same boat.

stories.summary: Seyi Tinubu, fils du chef de l’État nigérian, multiplie les alliances pour implanter le City Boy Movement dans le sud-est du pays. En recrutant milliardaires et transfuges politiques, il tente ainsi d’ébranler le fief de l’opposant et candidat à la présidentielle Peter Obi.

stories.summary: They face hurdles accessing education, healthcare, and other public services as they are considered foreigners.

stories.summary: CAF has been consistently behind Gianni Infantino who is seeking a controversial fourth term to 2031, despite criticism of his leadership.

stories.summary: Banque, mines, agro-industrie ou mobile money : au Mali, des femmes s’imposent à la tête d’entreprises et dans des secteurs stratégiques. Portraits.

stories.summary: Après dix-neuf ans de lieux d’accueil temporaires et d’incertitudes, la paroisse qui constitue un point d’ancrage pour les exilés de la guerre vient de trouver dans la capitale britannique un bâtiment permanent pour sa communauté.

stories.summary: La fille du fondateur de l’empire de la bière et du vin, Romy Castel, s’efforce d’évincer le directeur général, protégé par une structure juridique et capitalistique complexe. Elle a remporté, en octobre, une importante victoire judiciaire.

stories.title: Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Bola Tinubu (in red hat) would be 79 at the end of a second term, if he is re-elected By Mansur Abubakar Reporting from Abuja Published 22 November 2026 Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics. At 38, he is among the young people seeking elected office in a country where about 80% of the population is under 40. He hopes his age will stand in his favour as he campaigns for a seat in the state assembly in the northern Kano state in January's general elections. "Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future," Dalhatu tells the BBC. But Nigeria's political history suggests he faces an uphill battle. Since the return to civilian rule in 1999, Goodluck Jonathan has been the youngest person elected president, taking office at the age of 53.

stories.title: Nigeria: At least 24 Dead After Boat Capsizes
stories.summary: Nigeria: At least 24 Dead After Boat Capsizes Pixabay Life preserver. 22 November 2026 Deutsche Welle (Bonn) By Emmy Sasipornkarn with AFP, AP The boat carrying mourners for a funeral overturned in southern Nigeria. It was the latest in a series of deadly boat accidents in the country. A boat capsized in southern Nigeria , killing at least 24 people, the country's emergency agency said on Saturday. "So far, 24 bodies have been recovered from the scene of the incident, while search and rescue operations are ongoing," said Manzo Ezekiel, a spokesman for the National Emergency Management Agency. The boat was carrying mourners for a burial ceremony from the town of Ayama to Ukubie in the southern Bayelsa State on Friday when it sank. Boat reportedly suffered mechanical failure Authorities have not confirmed how many passengers were on board. "Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way," Nigerian President Bola Tinubu said in a statement on X.

stories.title: Belkacem, Ben Barka, Ben Youssef : ces assassinats politiques qui ont marqué les premières années post-indépendance au Maghreb
stories.summary: En octobre, au cimetière d’El-Alia dans la capitale algérienne, on commémorait timidement le 56e anniversaire du décès de Krim Belkacem, héros gommé du roman national pour s’être opposé au FLN. L’occasion de se souvenir que, dans les trois pays du Maghreb, les premières années d’indépendance ont été marquées par la violence politique.

stories.title: « Passer à l’offensive » : au Bénin, comment Romuald Wadagni muscle sa stratégie antiterroriste
stories.summary: Le chef de l’État béninois a désigné le colonel Claude Raoul Djèhoungo pour diriger l’opération Mirador. Alors que la menace s’étend vers le Nigeria, l’intensification de la réponse militaire permettra-t-elle de sortir de la crise sécuritaire ?

stories.title: Mushikiwabo maintenue un an à l’OIF, Tebboune reçoit l’émissaire de Macron, bataille budgétaire au Sénégal… Les 5 infos qu’il ne fallait pas manquer
stories.summary: Cette semaine, le Brief de Jeune Afrique revient sur ce qui s’est passé au sommet de la Francophonie à Phnom Penh, décrit le climat délétère qui règne à l’Assemblée nationale sénégalaise, envisage l’avenir minier de la Côte d’Ivoire, analyse les tensions diplomatiques soulevées par des expulsions d’orpailleurs au Sahel et dévoile la dernière tentative ratée de Paris pour se réconcilier avec Alger.

stories.title: ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
stories.summary: Image source, Gallo Images via Getty Images Image caption, The ANC got the most votes overall but lost control in more than half of the councils it won in 2021 Published 21 November 2026 The party that has dominated South Africa for more than 30 years is in a race against time to secure power-sharing deals in most of the country's cities after a massive drop in its support in this month's local elections. The African National Congress (ANC) suffered its worstâ¯result since it came to power in 1994 when South Africa transitioned from the racist apartheid system to democracy. It won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo, down from six in the last elections. It won the most votes in just two of the country's eight cities, compared with six in 2021. At the national level, the ANC is sharing power with its long-time rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA), but while there is still no official announcement, it appears that ANC party officials do not want to replicate this at the local level.

stories.title: Le Gabon obtiendra-t-il un programme avec le FMI d’ici à la fin de l’année ?
stories.summary: Le Gabon obtiendra-t-il un programme avec le FMI d’ici à la fin de l’année ? Le Gabon espère parvenir à un accord sur un nouveau programme avec le FMI dès décembre. stories.title: Zeinab Badawi : « L’Afrique a une histoire très riche, bien avant l’arrivée des Européens »
stories.summary: Zeinab Badawi : « L’Afrique a une histoire très riche, bien avant l’arrivée des Européens » La journaliste et historienne soudano-britannique Zeinab Badawi, autrice d’« Une histoire africaine de l’Afrique », souhaite que le continent puisse se réapproprier son propre récit. Son livre à succès jette un éclairage inédit sur les enjeux géopolitiques contemporains. Par Jeanne Le Bihan (Entretien) , Nicholas Norbrook (Entretien) , Fatma Ben Hamad (Réalisation) , et Christelle Pire (Tournage) Publié aujourd'hui à 18h01 Lecture : 1 minute. C’est ce qui l’a poussée à écrire.

stories.title: Minerais critiques : au Kenya, un consortium américain met la main sur un site prometteur

stories.title: Au Mali, une nouvelle société militaire turque épaule secrètement la junte d’Assimi Goïta
stories.summary: Des instructeurs d’Equipped Tactical Academy ont formé des éléments des forces spéciales maliennes, fin 2025. stories.title: Après l’exercice Jebel Sahara, où en est le partenariat militaire entre Rabat et Londres ?
stories.summary: Après l’exercice Jebel Sahara, où en est le partenariat militaire entre Rabat et Londres ? stories.summary: Un article de « Mediapart », publié jeudi 19 novembre, affirme qu’une société du judoka, candidat à la présidentielle, a bénéficié de commandes du souverain marocain « pour des millions d’euros ». Une enquête qui illustre les liens étroits qu’entretiennent les deux hommes.

stories.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
stories.summary: People watch a large wave break over the seawall in Pacifica, California Photograph: Fred Greaves/Reuters View image in fullscreen People watch a large wave break over the seawall in Pacifica, California Photograph: Fred Greaves/Reuters California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night.

stories.summary: L’expulsion de dizaines de milliers d’orpailleurs clandestins par le gouvernement de Conakry met à bas l’économie de toute une région dans le nord-est du pays. stories.title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Africa is pushing for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035, from an annual $40bn (Â£30bn) By Navin Singh Khadka Environmental correspondent, BBC World Service Published 20 November 2026 In Uganda's northern Karamoja region, Elijah Lobur and his family now eat just one meal a day. A severe drought that began in April has destroyed crops, while food brought in from elsewhere has become increasingly unaffordable. "Seven months without rain has brought us to this point where we now live in hunger," the 44-year-old farmer, who lives with his grandmother, wife and five children, told the BBC. "Even some of the wild plants that we used to eat have withered and dried up." Local officials say more than 90% of crops have failed in the region, where agriculture is largely rain-fed. Further south, in Malawi, Mathews Nkhambala has experienced the devastating effects of flooding. In April 2024, barely a year after Tropical Cyclone Freddy devastated the country's southern region, floods displaced people in Chikwawa district. Nkhambala fled to higher ground with his wife and four children as floodwaters swept through his village. "As we reached a safe height, we saw our house swept away right in front of our eyes.

stories.title: Mentors, colleagues and friends: tributes paid to the ‘Eritrea 16’ who disappeared 25 years ago

Photograph: Courtesy of CPJ Africa Mentors, colleagues and friends: tributes paid to the ‘Eritrea 16’ who disappeared 25 years ago Families of journalists who vanished into state prisons on ‘Black Tuesday’ in 2001 do not know whether they are even still alive When Fisseha Yirgalem stepped on to the podium and began reading from a letter written to a man who may never hear it, the room full of journalists in Nairobi fell quiet. The Eritrean writer’s personal tribute to Amanuel Asrat , a poet, writer, and founder of Zemen newspaper, was not merely about an abstract human rights case but about her mentor, former colleague and friend whose life had in effect been erased by the authoritarian state of Eritrea. Asrat is one of 16 journalists who disappeared into Eritrea’s prison system 25 years ago on Black Tuesday – 18 September 2001 – when the government shut down all of the newspapers in the country.

Photograph: Frank Dejongh/Unicef One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report. In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund ( UNFPA ) published on Thursday.

stories.title: Compromis à la francophonie, Bassirou Faye radié du Pastef, CAN 2027 : l'hebdo Afrique
stories.summary: Publicité Récap Compromis à la francophonie, Bassirou Faye radié du Pastef, CAN 2027 : l'hebdo Afrique Publié le : 20/11/2026 - 09:09 7 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 La secrétaire générale de la Francophonie, Louise Mushikiwabo, écoute les délégués lors de la cérémonie de clôture du 20e Sommet de la Francophonie, à Phnom Penh, au Cambodge, le 16 novembre 2026. © Soveit Yarn, Reuters Le Pastef, parti majoritaire au Sénégal dirigé par le président de l'Assemblée nationale Ousmane Sonko , a officialisé mardi le départ de ses rangs du président Bassirou Diomaye Faye , en conflit avec son ancien Premier ministre, en pleine crise budgétaire entre l'exécutif et le Parlement. Une analyse de David Rich à lire sur France 24 . Près de 700 000 personnes ont été déplacées par des affrontements entre forces armées des régions Somali et de l'Oromia, qui font rage depuis près d'un mois dans le sud de l' Éthiopie , a annoncé jeudi l'ONG britannique Islamic Relief. Les premiers combats remontent à fin octobre, après qu'un drapeau de la région Somali a été hissé à Moyale, ville éthiopienne frontalière avec le Kenya , administrée conjointement par les deux régions éthiopiennes. Deux vaccins ciblant spécifiquement la souche d'Ebola qui sévit en République démocratique du Congo devraient faire l'objet d'essais cliniques sur place dès la semaine prochaine, a annoncé mardi l'Organisation mondiale de la santé.

Photograph: Danish Siddiqui/Reuters Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay , if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya. ‘They showed no mercy’: mapping the Rohingya villages being erased by rebel forces Read more The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group. Lawyers representing Rohingya survivors say patterns of behaviour by Myanmar’s military, including killing people as they fled, show clear attempts to destroy the group during assaults on Rakhine state in 2016 and 2017. It is the role of independent judges to interpret the genocide convention.

She is thinking about getting around more easily. The railway runs through Catumbela, near the Angolan city of Lobito, on the Atlantic coast. For Julia, it has made travelling cheaper and more convenient. "Before, I had to use a taxi, which is much more expensive. Now it is cheaper and easier to travel," she says.

The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen , the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

Photograph: K Desouki/AFP/Getty ‘I’m not ready to go to jail’: co-founder of Egypt’s last independent media outlet faces prison Mada Masr, the news site co-founded by Lina Attalah just before the 2013 military coup, is fighting for its life after being shut down, but its journalists have not given up hope F acing a year in prison for running Egypt’s leading independent news outlet Mada Masr , Lina Attalah is trying to focus on the everyday: waking at dawn to hear the birds sing before Cairo’s streets come alive and visiting Mada Masr’s shuttered offices with her reporters to water the plants and feed their four cats. Attalah is the reluctant face of Egypt’s embattled independent press at a moment of crisis. In the last six weeks, Egyptian authorities have waged a renewed crackdown on the few remaining independent media outlets left in the country, beginning with the arrest of the entire newsroom of the factchecking website Matsadaash.

stories.title: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda
stories.summary: The Danish PM, Mette Frederiksen (centre), Austrian chancellor Christian Stocker (second left), and Rwandan minister Vincent Biruta (right) in Vienna on Monday. Photograph: Leonhard Föger/Reuters View image in fullscreen The Danish PM, Mette Frederiksen (centre), Austrian chancellor Christian Stocker (second left), and Rwandan minister Vincent Biruta (right) in Vienna on Monday. Photograph: Leonhard Föger/Reuters Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’ Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”. The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country. In a statement released on Monday the five EU countries said “concrete negotiations with partner country Rwanda will begin for implementation”, saying the scheme would make “an important contribution to further curbing illegal migration, dismantling the business model of smugglers and relieving the burden on our population”.

stories.title: BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa
stories.summary: Image source, Ifiokabasi Ettang/BBC Image caption, Hadiza left school at 13 to get married and now spends her time doing housework By Madina Maishanu BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Goronyo Published 17 November 2026 As she pounds millet, 15-year-old Hadiza sings the English alphabet. It is a reminder of something that she desperately misses - going to school. "Sometimes I write on the ground to practise and see if I'm still writing correctly," she says. One night, about two years ago, a group of armed men raided her village. "They scared our cattle away and abducted a girl. We walked barefoot all the way here," she says. Since then she has lived in a displaced persons camp in Goronyo, a few kilometres from her home.
